title: King and Pawn — Direct Opposition
description: White has a king and pawn vs lone Black king. To promote the pawn, White must use the king aggressively. The key concept is Opposition.
explanation: White must advance the king in front of the pawn. Key idea: take the opposition — place your king directly opposite the enemy king with a single square between them. With the opposition, you can push the enemy king back. Play Kd2 then Ke3-Ke4-Ke5 with the pawn following.

title: King and Pawn — Triangulation
description: White appears to be in zugzwang, but can use triangulation to lose a tempo and gain the opposition. A key endgame technique.
explanation: Triangulation: White's king takes 3 moves to reach the same square it started on, while Black's king can only take 2 moves. This loses Black a tempo. Play Kd3-Kd2-Kc2-Kd3? No — the correct triangle is Kb3-Kb2-Kc2-Kd3 (or Kd2-Kc2-Kb3-Kb4-Kc4). The king 'triangulates' to achieve the same position but with Black to move.

title: Lucena Position
description: The Lucena Position is the most important winning position in rook endgames. White must 'build a bridge' to shelter the king from checks.
explanation: The Lucena technique ('building a bridge'): 1.Re4! (preparing to shelter the king) Rg2 (or any check) 2.Kc7 Rc2+ 3.Kb6 Rb2+ 4.Kc6 Rc2+ 5.Rc4!! (the bridge) Rxc4+ 6.Kb5 Rc8 7.b8=Q. The rook on c4 blocks the file, shielding the king from checks long enough to promote.

title: Philidor Position (Defence)
description: Black must hold the Philidor Position draw against White's rook and advanced pawn. This is the defensive technique to a Lucena-like attack.
explanation: Philidor's technique: Black keeps the rook on the 6th rank (1...Re6), cutting off the White king. Only when the pawn advances to e6 does Black switch to checking from behind: ...Ra6-Ra5-Ra1 (checking from behind the pawn). With the rook on e2, Black demonstrates the correct Philidor draw: 1...Re6! 2.Rc1 Ra6+ 3.Kb5 Ra1 and Black checks from behind endlessly.

title: Rook vs Advanced Pawn
description: Black has a pawn on b2, one step from promotion. White's king and rook must hold the draw. Precise technique required!
explanation: White draws by cutting off the Black king and checking from the side. 1.Kc2 Ka5 2.Rd8! (threatening Ra8+ and Rb8) ...b1=Q+ 3.Kxb1 draws. Key idea: the White rook on d8 controls everything. If instead 1...b1=Q+ 2.Rxb1 Kxb1 stalemate — wait, that loses. Correct is 1.Kc2 then Rd8 attacking from distance.

title: Wrong-Colour Bishop
description: Black has a h-pawn and king. White has only a bishop — but it is the wrong colour! Demonstrate the famous drawing technique.
explanation: Bishop and rook pawn are a draw when the bishop doesn't control the promotion square. Black just needs to reach the corner: 1...h1=Q+? No: 1...Kh1! 2.Bf2 stalemate — but the pawn is already on h2! So: 1...Kh2 2.Bg3+ Kh1! and it's stalemate (or 2.Bf2 h1=Q+ 3.Bxh1 — draw, but wrong king position). The correct method: Black keeps the king on h1/g1 to force stalemate after Bxh1. Key lesson: h1 rook pawn with wrong-colour bishop = automatic draw.

title: Two Bishops vs King
description: White has two bishops — together they form an unstoppable mating network. Drive the Black king to the corner.
explanation: Two bishops force mate by driving the king to a corner using a 'staircase' technique. The bishops work together to cover adjacent diagonals. Plan: 1.Bd3+ Ke5 2.Bc4 Kd4 3.Bf2 Kc5 4.Kh2 Kb4 5.Be3 Ka5 6.Bc5 Ka6 7.Bb4 Ka7 8.Bd6 Kb8 9.Bd5 Kc8 10.Ba6 (threatening Bb7#) Kd8 11.Bb6#. Take your time — don't rush.

title: Queen vs Pawn on 7th
description: White's queen must stop the Black d-pawn from promoting. Demonstrate the technique to win with queen vs pawn on the 7th rank.
explanation: The queen stops the pawn by checking the king repeatedly to bring the White king closer. 1.Qh4+ Ke8 (if Kd8 2.Qb4 Kc8 3.Qb7+ Ka8 4.Kd2 Ka7 5.Kc3 Ka6 6.Kc4! — king marches up) 2.Qe4+ Kd8 3.Qb4! (forces the king to block its own pawn) Ke8 4.Kd2 and White's king approaches. Don't sacrifice prematurely!

title: Pawn Breakthrough
description: Black has three pawns vs three pawns, all locked up. But one side can break through! Find the breakthrough sacrifice.
hints: Sometimes you must sacrifice pawns to create a passed pawn
Which pawn sacrifice creates an unstoppable promotion?
explanation: Wait — it's Black to move but Black has pawns on a7,c7,e7 vs White's a5,c5,e5. Actually White's pawns are advanced. Let me reconsider: 1...b5! (Black actually needs ...e5 or ...c5). In this mirror position: whichever side sacrifices correctly wins. The breakthrough: if Black plays 1...e5 2.axb6 cxb6 3.c6 bxc6 4.e6 and one pawn queens first.

title: Rook Endgame — Active King
description: White has a slight advantage with a rook. The key principle: in rook endgames, activate your king! A passive king loses. Show the technique.
explanation: White should activate the king immediately: 1.Kf3! Kf6 2.Ke4 Ke6 3.Rf3! (threatening to invade) g5 4.Kf4 Kd5 5.Kg5 Ke4 6.Kxg6 Kxf3 7.Kxf7 Ke4 8.Kg6 Kf4 9.f3 and White's f-pawn queens. The principle: in rook endgames, the king is your most powerful piece — march it to the centre immediately!
